absent: Mapper callback contract for get_block beyond mapped, new, boundary and up to date outcomes.
Namespace semaphore acquisition and mount hash and tree insertion and removal rules.
Writeback iterator error and retry semantics and cgroup accounting details.
Buffer head lifecycle and folio buffer creation and free thresholds.
Audit registration effects for completed filenames.
Sysctl default values and enforcement logic for protected link and fifo modes.
RCU reclamation path for mounts and namespace passive reference drop timing.
End of device guard failure handling and BIO error propagation beyond folio marking.

findings.text: Mount record aggregates hierarchy, sharing, identity and reclamation state. Ancestry uses mnt_parent with child and sibling linkage, while lookup uses hash membership and namespace tree membership. A shared union serves tree versus deferred cleanup roles. Peer sharing, slave lists and master backpointers model propagation. Device naming, namespace, mountpoint, visibility, pins, covers and overmount track attachment and leftover coverage. Flags and numeric identifiers track grouping, expiry and reuse.

Proc mounts iterator bundles a namespace reference with a root path and a show callback. The namespace selects which mount set is walked, the path anchors display relative to a root, and the callback formats one mount entry into a sequence output.

Read aggregation arguments carry the target folio and allowed page count, plus readahead mode, in-progress BIO, contiguity tracker, mapping scratch space, logical start of cached mapping, and block resolution callback. Together they allow reuse of a prior mapping across calls and accumulation of contiguous blocks into one BIO.

Write aggregation state is smaller than the read state. It keeps the in-progress BIO, the last block already placed for contiguity checks, and the block resolution callback used when a folio lacks buffers.

Name lookup state bundles current and root paths, final component, current inode, lookup and state flags, several sequence counters for retry validation, terminal component classification, nesting depth and link count. Symlink traversal uses a stack pointer with inline storage for a few levels. It also carries the filename object, original pathname, saved outer state, directory descriptor and directory identity and mode.

Containing namespace and the t-flag word are owned by the namespace semaphore. The namespace pointer may additionally be read without that semaphore under RCU, but such readers must not assume continued activity and only gain an implicit passive hold via the RCU grace delay before deactivation drops its reference.

Crossing to a parent mount takes the mount seqlock in exclusive read mode, samples parent and mountpoint under the lock with reference holds, then releases before swapping the caller path. Root mounts with self parentage return without change.

Mount propagation uses distinct mark bits for shared, unbindable, internal traversal marking and unmount candidacy. Becoming shared clears only the unbindable subset, preserving other marks. The hold marker is reserved for writer hold logic on the superblock predecessor link.
Superblock sibling linkage steals the low bit of the predecessor pointer for hold state, so the stored predecessor is not a plain pointer and must be decoded with that reservation in mind.

Read mapping prefers reusing a cached extent before invoking the filesystem mapper, requires strict physical contiguity within a folio BIO, zeroes hole regions, completes fully hole folios without I/O, and otherwise falls back to the generic full folio path on any disorder such as noncontiguity, hole to data transition, preexisting buffers or mapper supplied up to date data.

Write mapping accepts only fully usable buffered folios with mapped dirty and valid blocks in contiguous order, else it falls back. Unbuffered folios are mapped block by block with new block alias handling. Folios wholly beyond size are not allocated backing, straddling tails are zeroed beyond size, and only the mapped prefix length is submitted.

Symlink nesting depth is bounded by inline levels plus dynamic extension. The stack pointer normally refers to inline storage and the saved entry preserves link path, completion callback, name and sequence for resumption.
Name cache storage is a slab cache pointer fixed after early init and accessed through a runtime constant wrapper, so lookup-time filename allocation uses a stable cache without further rebinding.
Terminal name classification distinguishes four cases: ordinary final component, root itself, single dot and double dot. Callers use this to select root, self and parent handling during final lookup.

Protected symlink, hardlink, fifo and regular file controls are exposed as integer sysctls under the fs namespace with read write permissions for owner and read for others, using bounded integer handlers with lower bound zero and upper bound one or two depending on control.

Readahead entry iterates folios from the readahead control, applies a tolerant allocation policy, accumulates contiguous reads into a shared BIO and submits any remainder at the end, stopping early if a folio ends unlocked and not valid.

Synchronous folio read entry processes a single folio through the same mapping and BIO batching logic, then submits any pending BIO and reports success unconditionally because errors surface through folio state.

Bulk writeback entry plugs the block layer, iterates dirty folios, optionally offers each to a filesystem handler and otherwise uses the multipage writer with shared BIO state, then submits any trailing BIO and returns the last iteration status.

User pathname acquisition translates empty path user flag into an internal empty lookup allowance. One variant may return null for empty input after a cheap initial probe to avoid allocation, and treats zero length names as absent.

Delayed filename helpers separate allocation from audit accounting. They can capture from user memory with or without empty allowance, adopt a uniquely referenced filename or copy a shared one, then either abandon the pending value or publish it with audit registration.

Magic link jump replaces the current lookup path with a supplied target after rejecting disallowed modes, records that a jump occurred, and transfers references so the old path is released and the new path owned. Failure releases the supplied target.
Parent crossing entry moves a path to its mountpoint in the parent mount when not already at a root, using locked sampling of parent state and reference exchange on success.

Read BIO lifecycle starts empty, allocates on first mappable folio with sector derived from first block, appends while physical contiguity holds, submits on discontinuity, boundary or capacity miss with retry on fresh BIO, and ends with completion marking each folio according to BIO status before release.

Write BIO lifecycle similarly accumulates contiguous mapped folios, submits on discontinuity or add failure, clears buffer dirtiness only after successful BIO membership, starts writeback and unlocks, then either submits immediately on boundary or hole-truncated folios with separate boundary block handling or extends the contiguity tracker. Errors on fallback are recorded against the mapping.

Delayed filename moves from uninitialized to incomplete after capture, then to exactly one terminal outcome: dismissed with release, or completed with audit and handover of ownership. Shared inputs are duplicated so the pending value remains exclusively owned.

Lookup jump state adds a jumped mark on success and preserves no other flag changes in this fragment. Callers can later distinguish paths that arrived via jump from ordinary traversal for scoped and special handling.

Low bit stealing on the superblock predecessor, RCU visibility of possibly deactivating namespaces, differing SMP counter storage, and leftover cover tracking create use after free, misdecode and accounting risks if locks, RCU discipline and build specific accessors are not respected.

End of device guarding, hole zeroing, beyond size truncation, boundary block flushing, and opportunistic buffer reclamation interact with concurrent reads. Clearing dirtiness before BIO membership, freeing buffers on non valid folios, or missing size checks can lose data or expose stale contents.

Jump must reject scoped lookups and magiclink disabled or cross device disallowed modes before any path swap. User name handling must validate user memory access and empty name semantics to avoid faults or wrong null versus error distinction.

Writer hold marker has value one. Propagation bits have values one, two, four and eight for shared, unbindable, internal mark and unmount candidate respectively, and the mask cleared on becoming shared equals the unbindable bit alone.
Inline symlink depth is two. Root preset, root grabbed and jumped state bits have values one, two and four respectively.
Internal namespace sentinel is a distinct invalid error pointer value that never equals a real namespace address, used to mark mounts outside any namespace.

Four sysctl names exist for protected symlinks, hardlinks, fifos and regular files, each with owner write and world read permissions, integer range starting at zero and ending at one for link controls and two for fifo and regular controls.
Multipage helpers expose readahead, single folio read and bulk writeback entry points for filesystems using block mapping callbacks, hiding BIO batching and fallback to generic full folio paths.
Pathname helpers expose user acquisition with empty path handling, delayed capture and completion or dismissal, plus path jump and parent crossing for lookup traversal.
